Dear Ed:
There are several comments relevant to the Draft Environmental Statement (DES 72-44) on the Proposed Endangered Species Conservation Act of 1972 which we feel should be made.
The bill evidently would place full responsibility for rare or endangered species management in the hands of the federal government and "...in effect remove listed species from the states' jurisdiction." (Page 6, second paragraph.) There is no justification for this action. If a state fails to assume the responsibility of managing such forms, within a reasonable period, there might then be a basis for such federal control. Native species of wildlife resident within a state have historically been considered the property of the state and subject to the laws of the state.
In the third paragraph of the section headed "Alternatives" it refers to "...selective imposition of the sanctions authorized by this bill...". The sanctions which might be imposed are not listed but usually involve withholding of federal support for one or more programs. As an example, the President's message to Congress dated February 8 1972 (Document No. 92-247) on Environmental Protection, suggested a National Land Use Policy Act amendment requiring states to control siting of major transportation facilities.
